build.description: Builds the Next.js app. TWO THINGS HERE ARE NOT WHAT THEY LOOK LIKE. (1) The ^build tasks execute nothing -- no other package has a build script -- and are load-bearing anyway: they carry each dependency's source hash into this task, which is what makes an edit in packages/ui invalidate this build. Deleting the line as dead config would introduce the stale-cache bug it appears to already have. (2) globalDependencies is not decoration: the apps/web -> root -> base tsconfig chain sits ABOVE the package boundary, so without it an edit to tsconfig.base.json leaves this hash unmoved and turbo restores a build made under the previous compiler options. Both were measured. DO NOT grow this key for tasks that do not consume these files: globalDependencies feeds the GLOBAL hash, and a task cannot opt out of it -- `!$TURBO_ROOT$/biome.jsonc` in this task's inputs was measured failing to exclude it. Adding biome.jsonc here for a future lint task would make every lint-config edit rebuild the app. Per-task inputs, or futureFlags.globalConfiguration's `global.inputs`, is where files only some tasks consume belong.
